issues.description: The Pneumatic.openValve method has inconsistent parameters across artifacts: the UML/problem statement declares openValve() with no parameters (problem_statement.md), but the solution's Pneumatic interface declares openValve(int duration) while the solution implementations (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement openValve() with no parameters. The template Pneumatic.java is empty. This mismatch between the specified interface and the solution implementation will confuse students and can cause compilation errors or unclear expectations about the correct method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Pneumatic.openValve signature consistent with the UML/problem statement (no parameters). Change the solution's Pneumatic interface to declare void openValve() and ensure all implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) override openValve() with no parameters. Also update the template Pneumatic.java to include the correct method signatures (void raisePressure(int) and void openValve()). Alternatively, if the intended design requires a duration parameter, update the UML/problem statement and all implementing classes to use openValve(int duration) consistently.
